parameters.query:
-- Store one review and decide, in the database, whether a human needs to see it.
--
-- The rating is authoritative: a number the customer chose cannot be talked out of by a model.
-- The model's sentiment only breaks the tie at 3 stars, or stands alone when someone left words
-- and no rating at all.
WITH p AS (
  SELECT $1::text AS booking_ref, $2::int AS rating, $3::text AS comment, $4::text AS hint,
         $5::text AS user_key
), appt AS (
  -- Only the customer's OWN completed appointment. Reviewing someone else's, or one that never
  -- happened, is not a review.
  SELECT a.* FROM appointment a
  JOIN client c ON c.id = a.client_id
  WHERE a.ref = (SELECT booking_ref FROM p)
    AND c.channel || ':' || c.channel_user_id = (SELECT user_key FROM p)
), checks AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM appt) > 0 AS found,
    (SELECT status FROM appt) AS status,
    COALESCE((SELECT rating FROM p) IS NULL
             OR (SELECT rating FROM p) BETWEEN 1 AND 5, false) AS rating_ok,
    COALESCE(btrim((SELECT comment FROM p)) <> '' OR (SELECT rating FROM p) IS NOT NULL, false) AS has_content,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM review r, appt WHERE r.appointment_id = appt.id) AS already_reviewed
), verdict AS (
  SELECT CASE
    WHEN (SELECT rating FROM p) >= 4 THEN 'praise'
    WHEN (SELECT rating FROM p) <= 2 THEN 'complaint'
    -- 3 stars, or words with no stars: the model's read is the only signal there is.
    WHEN (SELECT hint FROM p) IN ('praise','complaint') THEN (SELECT hint FROM p)
    ELSE 'neutral'
  END AS sentiment
), ins AS (
  INSERT INTO review (appointment_id, client_id, stylist_id, rating, comment, sentiment, escalated_at)
  SELECT a.id, a.client_id, a.stylist_id, p.rating, NULLIF(btrim(p.comment), ''), v.sentiment,
         CASE WHEN v.sentiment <> 'neutral' THEN now() END
  FROM appt a, p, verdict v, checks c
  WHERE c.found AND c.status = 'completed' AND c.rating_ok AND c.has_content AND NOT c.already_reviewed
  RETURNING id, appointment_id, sentiment, rating, comment
)
SELECT json_build_object(
  'found', (SELECT found FROM checks), 'status', (SELECT status FROM checks),
  'rating_ok', (SELECT rating_ok FROM checks), 'has_content', (SELECT has_content FROM checks),
  'already_reviewed', (SELECT already_reviewed FROM checks),
  'stored', (SELECT count(*) FROM ins) > 0,
  'review', (SELECT json_build_object(
      'id', i.id, 'appointment_id', i.appointment_id, 'sentiment', i.sentiment,
      'rating', i.rating, 'comment', i.comment,
      'stylist_name', st.name, 'client_name', c.name, 'service_name', sv.name,
      'ref', a.ref,
      'when_local', to_char(a.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila', 'Dy DD Mon, HH24:MI'))
    FROM ins i
    JOIN appointment a ON a.id = i.appointment_id
    JOIN stylist st ON st.id = a.stylist_id
    JOIN service sv ON sv.id = a.service_id
    JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = a.client_id)
) AS result;

parameters.content:
## 41 · tool: submit review

**In** `{booking_ref, rating, comment, sentiment, user_key}` · **Out** `{ok:true,data}` or `{ok:false,reason}`

The **rating decides** — 4+ is praise, 2- is a complaint. A model's read of the words only breaks the tie at 3 stars, or stands alone when someone left words and no stars. A number the customer chose is not something a model gets to reinterpret.

Only the customer's OWN completed appointment can be reviewed, and only once.

Praise AND complaints both reach the manager, verbatim — you cannot coach a team on complaints alone. Neutral is stored and left alone.

`reason`: `invalid_input` · `invalid_rating` · `booking_not_found` · `not_completed` · `empty_review` · `already_reviewed` · `db_unavailable`
